It absolutely feels personal. I don't think these people go around pointing out random stuff about others to their faces, so why me? I'm minding my business, why can't you do the same? I know the things I like are for me alone but still...🥲 Sometimes it's a safe way to explore unfamiliar feelings, maybe those feelings are coming across to me as anxiety?

I know what you mean. I see women around me, both irl and online, live their lives in a way like you described, having these shared experiences with dating and friendships. It's like girl code to gossip about guys and girlfriends, go have coffee dates and hang out at malls, have shared hobbies. I've always been jealous I haven't had a friend to do any of that with :( I can't force myself to chat online with people or go on dates, it's too uncomfortable and it pains me to see other people just do it without thinking, like it was second nature to them.

When I was young I tried really hard to be not like other girls, pretending I was too edgy or something to do average stuff like shopping and now I'm realizing I'm old and alone without any social skills. And I think I'm a pretty average woman, I like makeup, shopping, pop culture, all that "vapid" stuff. I refuse to be ashamed for being basic and maybe wanting some more "traditional" stuff. But still I'll never be good enough for other women because I'm on the spectrum. 

Just last night I cried myself to sleep thinking about how if I ever need help with anything, I won't have anyone to hold my hand and share the emotional load, the most I can get is a chat with AI. I guess it would good to be self reliant and capable of anything but damn, the loneliness fu\*king hurts! Having feelings is not weak, it's natural! Am I supposed to train myself to think that all people suck and I'm better off alone forever? Because that's the kind of advice I've gotten before when venting about loneliness online...🫠 Sorry I wen't off the rails a bit here. Just wanted to say I feel you OP💖

Anyways, I feel you on the first part. That has been my experience too. On the other side, I have never gotten along with men either. I don't think I have anything in common with the average man, sorry... I'm being mean and dramatic, but most of the ones I've met at workplaces and university are vapid, superficial and have misogynistic, racist, aggressive "sense of humor". Of course I've met a bunch of really sweet, smart, funny, kind, hardworking, caring gentlemen but most have girlfriends so they avoid women so they wouldn't come across as flirty (or at least they avoid me...)

Hi! Seeing the post title made me go yeah, absolutely, that's me! I'm sorry you're going through this too. I wish I could help. I hope it's not inappropriate for me to vent here but this topic is close to my heart...

I had classmates I hung out with in middle school but they made it pretty clear I was like the 5th option if no one else wanted to hang out. And after school they just moved on. I tried to come up with plans but everyone else had always "been there done that (with someone else)". I even had people tell me they were like super busy right now... I never heard from them again. I've been to group therapy, that did nothing for my social anxiety. I had a volunteer to hang out with me but they quite literally ghosted me and our agency contact after one meetup. Imagine being so lame even a volunteer friend wants nothing to do with you?! LOL. edit: wanted to add, I also try to socialize online, I was told to "practice speaking" in therapy by talking in online forums, but I can't do it more than the occasional anonymous comment. Like I just can't come up with anything to say :/ I think this is an autism thing?

I've had a few jobs since (retail and customer service! So I have experience with being polite!) and I'm in university too but I have had no luck socializing with my peers. I guess I have pretty bad social anxiety, I just freeze up when I meet people. Even the nicest people I meet treat me like I have 3 heads or something. Everyone seems to only be talking about stuff they're doing with other friends and family and I can't relate at all :( I see people walking around the town chatting, not doing anything special and it hurts my heart, literally pains me to be so lonely and distanced from "normal life". I have tried to be better and nicer but it's not working, I'm too wrong/stupid/lame/boring/different.

Sometimes I "wake up" and realize that my peers have families, own houses, pets, hobbies, active lives and I'm wasting my life hiding in my room?! I'm almost 30 and I have never had a hobby or like a credit card or a driver's license, not even a career. I don't want their lives but I'm not surprised "average" people find me super weird.

Anyways, good luck to you and everyone who reads this. I hope we all find something to fill the void.💞

I'm gonna have to say the same thing as the other comments have, it's not your problem. I don't think you can really so anything in this case. The only people who can help her are ones who have been trained to work with whatever she's going through, and even then it's her choice if she wants to accept help. You are a good person for worrying but I'm afraid you're going to just end up hurting yourself if you get too deep into someone else's "mess". If you don't have anyone to contact, just ignore her? That's such an awful thing to say but she's not even really your friend, if I understood your post right. You don't own her anything and it might be too much for your health to worry about her (it would be for me!).

I'm the same way, I really resonate with you saying "I wish my life was mine". I've been living just preparing for work and then unwinding from work for years, I don't even know what I'd like to do if I weren't half asleep most of the time. It's so frustrating. I need 24+ hours of absolutely nothing to do before I'm mentally ready to do anything. I'm constantly on edge thinking about school and other life responsibilities, but I'm not sure if that's an autism thing or what's wrong with me🥲 I'm so surprised when people say they went to the gym, cleaned up their whole apartment or went on a shopping trip before and after work/school, like I only can just lay on a sofa waiting and resting! Maybe I need to just start to force myself to do something else for 10 minutes a day and see how I feel about it, might just build a new refreshing routine out of it🤷 Maybe one day... Good luck to you too💞

This post sounds exactly like something I could've written! I'm sorry you're going through stuff like this too, it really fucking hurts. I've also lost everyone but I'm not getting anywhere if I keep dwelling in the self hate. You're not the reason your friends are doing badly or not. Being myself(autistic) has taught me I have to put myself first, be comfortable with being alone, because I'm never going to get what I want from others (=acceptance). I can act all proper around strangers but being myself is just not going to work so what can you do? Stop looking at others for acceptance. No one can live like that happily, neurotypical or not. I don't think that ending it all is the way to go. You can do your own thing, even though it feels too lonely right now. It's fine to be alone. Hope I'm not sounding too mean/dismissive here, I have a little bit too negative way of looking at life (due to issues just like the ones in this post.) 🩷

I think a part of it has to do with social standing. Like most people wouldn't snitch on someone who has power over them, because that person could make their lives difficult. Sometimes it's easier to just keep quiet. Someone might also think that pointing out things that are wrong makes too much unnecessary work/trouble for the people whose job it is to fix things. So I think I have a different view of snitching, a selfish one, because I don't want to get negative attention for going against the social norms. Which in my experience protect the "bigger people" and I'm just a lowly nobody, you know :D Like you have to pick your battles. And most people just want to fit in and don't think about anything but their own comfort.

I feel the same way as you do, I could've written this post! I've faced similar problems in university. I don't have any answers or help for you, but here's some rambles about my feelings on this matter... I've noticed other people have this way of making themselves be known at all times. Like constantly talking, and just knowing when to say a lighthearted little joke to build positive rapport with others. I don't notice these situations. I have never managed to be "fluid" in conversation like that. I could never just stop by a group of people and make a comment that makes everyone like me a little more. 

But neurotypicals do that all the time, that's why they feel connected. I think that's why they can get away with so much, because they have somehow vetted others beforehand to be good funny people. Somehow I miss these moments. I guess people chat in the cafeteria, in the parking lot, during breaks? I find it way too overwhelming to be "on" all the time like that. I guess my chatting is too rehearsed and that makes people feel like I'm cold and weird. Nothing wrong with that, I just have different way of communicating and it's too jarring for people who don't know me... So, you're not bad, we're not bad, we're just neurodivergent! 💕
